elements.element: Renewal requires mutual written agreement unless every conditional automatic-renewal element below is met.
elements.evidence: Section 4.1 as rendered still provides that the Agreement "shall be automatically renewed for an additional one year period on each anniversary of the Effective Date"; there is no mutual-written-agreement renewal, and the conditional automatic-renewal elements are not all satisfied (opt-out is 60 rather than 30 days and no Vendor reminder exists), so the gateway element fails.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, each renewal term is no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: "automatically renewed for an additional one year period on each anniversary of the Effective Date" — a 12-month renewal term, unchanged by the redline.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer may opt out on no more than 30 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Rendered text requires "terminated by the Company upon sixty (60) days ... prior written notice"; 60 days exceeds the preferred 30-day maximum. To reach preferred, the Company's figure must be reduced to thirty (30) days.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Vendor must remind Customer at least 60 days before renewal.
elements.evidence: Neither Section 4.1 nor any other rendered language imposes any pre-renewal reminder obligation on HDI; the drafter did not insert one and the margin comment does not promise one.

elements.element: If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at the lesser of CPI and 3 percent.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: Section 3.1 sets a fixed consideration of "thirty percent (30%) of the Net Sales in excess of Eleven Thousand Dollars ($11,000) per calendar month" with no renewal-term uplift or price-adjustment mechanic anywhere in the cited text, so no cap is required.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer's non-renewal notice window is no more than 60 days.
elements.evidence: Amended Section 4.1 reads "unless terminated by the Company upon sixty (60) days, or by HDI upon ninety (90) days, prior written notice to the other" — Customer's (the Company's) window is exactly 60 days, within the fallback maximum; the deterministic check confirms this after alias normalization.

elements.element: If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at 5 percent.
elements.evidence: Condition not engaged: the fee is a fixed 30% revenue share above an $11,000 monthly threshold with no uplift-on-renewal provision, so there is no price increase to cap. (The mapping's "already_met" quote of Section 3.1 is inapt evidence — that clause contains no cap — but the element is satisfied because the trigger is absent.)

reasons: Fallback level is position-complete: the Customer-side non-renewal/termination notice is now 60 days, and the price-cap element is inapplicable because the fixed 30%-of-Net-Sales fee contains no renewal uplift mechanic.

Preferred level fails on three counts the drafter would have to fix in operative text: (i) Customer's opt-out is 60 days, not "no more than 30 days"; (ii) no clause obliges HDI to give Customer a reminder at least 60 days before each renewal; (iii) consequently the mutual-written-agreement gateway is not excused.

Minimality holds: the only substantive change is bifurcating the single 90-day notice figure into 60 days for the Company and 90 days for HDI. Retaining HDI's 90-day notice is Customer-favourable and correctly preserved; the 12-month renewal term, the "Termination Date" definition, and Section 3.1 are untouched. The added word "prior" in "prior written notice" is a grammatical consequence of splitting the two notice periods and does not alter meaning or add a requirement.

Intent preserved: the amended sentence remains grammatical ("to the other" still resolves between the two named Parties), the "Termination Date" definition in the following sentence still has an antecedent notice, and no cross-reference or commercial mechanic is left dangling or contradicted.

The "deviation" classification is correct: the original 90-day window exceeded the 60-day fallback maximum (though it sat below the 90-day walk-away threshold), so a redline was warranted rather than a rationale-only note.

Drafting note for the margin comment: it accurately describes the change; if the team wants the preferred position it should ask for 30 days plus an HDI reminder obligation 60 days before each anniversary, and say so as the ask with 60 days offered as the fallback.
